RFRed Fox9m ago

Lead with the recommendation; the finding can follow.

The river

The river , and both times the footbridge held. The second rise came within a hand of the deck boards, which is closer than any year since the bridge was rebuilt.

MLMaya Lindqvist3m ago

Was it twice? The log says once, on the 14th.

We recommend raising the deck by one course before the spring melt. The cost is modest and the work can be done in two days with the water low.

MLMaya Lindqvist5m ago

Two days is optimistic. Last time the same job took a week; say so, or give a range.

The path

RFRed Foxjust now

Walkers need a sign here before the meadow is gone.

The path on the north bank is washed out for about twenty metres. Walkers are cutting across the meadow, which is doing more harm than the river did.

Prompt to build this component

When to use it

When to use

  • To show a key or a key combination people press, inside a sentence or a hint line: "Press ⇧ ⌥ C to comment".
  • One key per element; a combination is several keys side by side, in the order they are held.

When not to use

  • For a command people type in a terminal: use cmp-code-block, or the typography mono class inside a sentence.
  • For a button people click: use cmp-button.
  • As a decorative badge or a count: use cmp-status-pill or the meta text of the part it belongs to.
Variants, anatomy, accessibility, interaction and content rules

Variants

Not applicable: one look. A small raised key with a hairline edge and a slightly heavier bottom edge, sized to sit inside a line of body or small text. It uses the base face, whose key symbols read clearly at small sizes.

Anatomy

  • Root: <kbd class="ds-kbd"> holding one key's symbol or name: ⇧, ⌥, ⌘, C, Enter.
  • Each key of a combination is its own ds-kbd; they sit next to each other with a small gap that comes from the surrounding text's spaces.

Accessibility

  • The native kbd element tells assistive technology that this is keyboard input.
  • Symbols alone are not always read well: when the hint names a combination with symbols, say it once in words too, for example with a title on the hint or a visually hidden "Shift Option C".
  • Not interactive: it never takes focus.

Interaction

  • None. It is shown, never pressed; nothing animates (int-04, int-06).

Content rules

  • Use the platform's own symbols for modifier keys (⇧ Shift, ⌥ Option, ⌘ Command, ⌃ Control) and a capital letter for letter keys.
  • Name the keys in the order they are held, modifiers first.
  • One key per element; never write a whole combination in one key.

Do and don't

  • Do keep the hint short: "Press ⇧ ⌥ C to comment".
  • Do put the keys inside the sentence that says what they do.
  • Don't use keys as decoration or for anything that is not pressed.
  • Don't restyle a key to look like a button; it is not clickable.
Source: design-system/components/basic/cmp-kbd/
